correctness.summary: The classical perpendicular-chord locus gives the fixed diagonal-point distance from the incircle center. Elementary chord geometry then gives a constant sum of squared tangency chords and its full feasible segment. Combining this with the known bicentric area formula and diagonal-product identity yields the semiperimeter formula, from which both displayed Blundon-Eddy defect factorizations follow algebraically. Equality cases agree with the right-kite and isosceles tangential-trapezoid extremizers.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical chord-tangent constructions, Josefsson's tangency-chord and area formulas, known Blundon-Eddy bounds and side-difference factorizations, and recent contact-quadrilateral formulas were excluded from the novelty claim. No located source states the radius-only tangency-chord squared-sum, the complete squared-chord line-segment image, the radius recovery, the fixed outer/contact area ratio, or the two contact-diagonal Blundon-Eddy defect factorizations. Equivalent older folklore remains a substantive residual risk.

value.summary: The result supplies a compact coordinate description of a classical bicentric Poncelet family and turns the two sharp semiperimeter bounds into exact nonnegative geometric defects. It also gives direct recovery of the circumradius from the incircle and contact diagonals and an invariant area ratio with the contact quadrilateral.

limitations: Only convex Euclidean bicentric quadrilaterals are covered.
The squared tangency-chord segment is the image of the family and is not claimed to parametrize labeled members injectively.
No extension to general tangential quadrilaterals, ex-bicentric quadrilaterals, or higher Poncelet polygons is claimed.
Dorrie's full 1965 section, Scherrer's 1933 paper, and the full text of Hung 2024 were not directly inspected and remain the principal literature risks.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; equivalent formulas under older chord-tangent notation may exist.
